stories.title: Implement typed Skyscanner API client
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts that wraps the Skyscanner RapidAPI. The client must: (1) export a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor accepts { apiKey: string }; if apiKey is omitted, fall back to the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable — throw a descriptive Error if neither is present; (2) implement searchFlights(params: SearchParams): Promise<FlightResult[]> using the Node.js 18+ global fetch (no third-party HTTP library); (3) export TypeScript interfaces SearchParams { origin: string; destination: string; date: string; adults?: number } and FlightResult { price: number; currency: string; airline: string; departure: string; arrival: string; duration: number; stops: number }; (4) throw on HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, including the status code in the message; (5) throw a descriptive parse error when the response body does not match the expected shape. Also create src/skyscanner/client.test.ts with vitest tests that mock the global fetch — no real network calls. (6) Support an explicit mock mode: when the environment variable MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API is set to the exact string 'true', searchFlights must return deterministic fixture FlightResult[] data WITHOUT making any network call (no fetch invocation at all) — this is an opt-in-only behavior; when MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API is unset, empty, or any value other than 'true', searchFlights must behave exactly as it does today (real fetch call, real failures surfaced, no silent fallback to mock data on real-call failure).
acceptanceCriteria: Delegated to split children: SKY-002-a, SKY-002-b

specification.coordinatorNotes: Foundational story with downstream dependents SKY-003 and SKY-004. Mock mode design (MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API strict opt-in semantics) and error-handling contract (API key leakage in messages, parse-error vs HTTP-error discrimination) are architecturally significant and need openspec elaboration before speckit hardening. 18 ACs indicate high surface area — speckit must verify testability of mock-mode strictness, private-field encapsulation, and the no-silent-fallback invariant. Both agents required; openspec first to refine mock-mode state-machine and error taxonomy, then speckit to add security and edge-case guardrails.

agentContributions.notes: 18 ACs exceeds 12-Ac limit; both impl and test files present in technicalNotes.files. Split per rules 1 and 2: impl child owns client.ts (typescript-engineer), test child owns client.test.ts (test-engineer). ACs consolidated to stay within ≤8 per child.

Modified AC 8 (original #8): removed 'vi.stubGlobal or equivalent' and 'stubs/spies' implementation instructions; replaced with observable behavior statement about mocking fetch with restoration and no real network calls. Modified AC 15 (original #15): broadened from only HTTP 4xx/5xx errors to ALL errors thrown by SkyscannerClient (constructor, HTTP, parse, network) — the apiKey must never leak in any error message, not just HTTP errors. Modified AC 16 (original #16): removed 'verified in a test that stubs/spies on global fetch and asserts it was never invoked' — this is an implementation instruction; the observable outcome is simply that fetch is not invoked. Added AC 19: network-level fetch rejection handling — openspec covered HTTP 4xx/5xx and malformed body but missed the case where fetch itself throws (DNS failure, connection refused). Added AC 20: API key must only be transmitted via headers, never in URL/query params — security criterion to prevent key leakage in URLs or logs. All other openspec ACs retained unchanged as they were well-formed, observable, and non-overlapping.

stories.title: Implement flight search CLI entry point with formatted table output
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that accepts flight search arguments via `process.argv` and prints results as an aligned table. Split into impl (cli.ts) and test (cli.test.ts) children.
acceptanceCriteria: Delegated to split children: SKY-003-impl, SKY-003-test

specification.coordinatorNotes: Requirements are already well-elaborated (15 ACs with precise exit-code, alignment, and formatting specs). No architectural ambiguity — openspec would add negligible value. speckit should harden testability criteria around table-alignment edge cases (wide Unicode currency symbols, empty-string fields), input-injection vectors in argv parsing, and verify the no-new-runtime-deps constraint is enforceable in CI. Single-agent run is sufficient.

agentContributions.notes: 15 ACs exceeds 12-AC limit; Rule 1 mandates split. Rule 2 also triggers (impl + test files in same story). Split into impl child (src/cli.ts, 8 ACs) and test child (src/cli.test.ts, 2 ACs). Impl ACs consolidated to hit ≤8 target without losing coverage.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Single-agent (speckit-only) run was appropriate — the original 15 ACs were already well-elaborated with precise exit codes, alignment rules, and formatting specs, so openspec elaboration would have been redundant. Speckit correctly split into impl (8 ACs) and test (8 ACs) children. All ACs are observable-behavior statements, non-overlapping, and testable. The impl ACs cover flag validation, date format, adults validation (including non-integer/≤0/empty), RAPIDAPI_KEY gating, table formatting with alignment rules, empty results, and error handling. The test ACs map 1:1 to the key behavioral scenarios. No implementation instructions leaked into test ACs. No security or edge-case gaps identified. Clean spec work.

stories.title: Build Express REST API with /health, /search, /cheapest, and static dashboard endpoints
stories.description: Create src/server.ts — an Express HTTP server exposing /health, /search, /cheapest, and a static dashboard (/). Server reads PORT (default 3000) and RAPIDAPI_KEY from env; gates /search and /cheapest with 503 if key absent. Depends on SKY-002. Split into three children: server implementation, dashboard + build config, and test suite.
acceptanceCriteria: Delegated to split children: SKY-004-impl, SKY-004-dashboard, SKY-004-test

specification.coordinatorNotes: Highest-complexity story: 4 endpoints, middleware gating pattern, static-file serving with build-pipeline coupling (tsc won't copy HTML), ESM/CJS listen-guard divergence, and dashboard HTML that must stay in sync with the filesystem. openspec must elaborate the middleware architecture (how RAPIDAPI_KEY absence gates only /search and /cheapest while /health and / remain open), the build-pipeline contract for static asset copying, and the interaction between SKY-002's mock mode and server-layer error propagation. speckit then reviews for testability (supertest isolation, mock-mode integration), security (error-message leakage, unhandled-rejection safety), and edge cases (concurrent requests during key rotation, missing dist/public after partial build). Both agents required; openspec first.

agentContributions.notes: 24 ACs exceeds 12 — mandatory split applied. Rule 2 triggered (impl + test files both present). Split into 3 children: (1) server routes/middleware impl, (2) dashboard HTML + build config, (3) test suite. Each child has ≤8 ACs.

src/public/index.html exists and is a real, styled single-page dashboard (not a placeholder) matching this concrete layout: (1) a full-width solid-color header bar (e.g. blue #1a73e8) containing a bold white title 'Skyscanner Dashboard' and a smaller subtitle line below it ('Search flights via the Skyscanner API' or equivalent); (2) below the header, a centered white card (max-width ~700px, rounded corners, light border, padding) containing a search form laid out as a 2-column grid: 'From (IATA)' and 'To (IATA)' text inputs on row 1, 'Date' (native date input) and 'Adults' (number input, default 1) on row 2, each with a label above the input; (3) a full-width solid-color button below the grid, same color as the header, labeled 'Search Flights'; (4) a status/message area below the button that shows a light-red/pink banner with red text for errors (e.g. 'Failed to fetch flights'), a muted-gray line for empty results ('No flights found'), and a result count on success; (5) client-side JavaScript that submits the form via GET /search (no full page reload), disables the button while the request is in flight, and renders returned flights into a results table (or the appropriate status message) in the same page

GET /search with valid query params (from, to, date, adults) returns HTTP 200 with body { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: ISO-8601 string } where count strictly equals flights.length
GET /search missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }
When the `adults` query param is absent on GET /search, the request succeeds (HTTP 200) with a default value of 1 passed to SkyscannerClient — `adults` is optional, not required
When the `adults` query param is present but non-numeric (e.g. 'abc', ''), GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

GET /cheapest with valid required query params (from, to, date) returns HTTP 200 with a single FlightResult whose `price` field is less than or equal to the `price` field of every FlightResult returned by SkyscannerClient for the same route/date (validated against a mocked client response); if `adults` is supplied it is forwarded, if absent it defaults to 1
GET /cheapest returns HTTP 404 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } when SkyscannerClient returns an empty array for the given route/date
GET /cheapest missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

When RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is absent at server initialisation, a single middleware (or equivalent) short-circuits GET /search and GET /cheapest with HTTP 503 Content-Type application/json body { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; GET /health and GET / are unaffected and return their normal responses

When SkyscannerClient throws an error during a /search or /cheapest request (e.g. network failure, upstream 5xx), the server returns HTTP 500 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } and does not crash or emit an unhandled promise rejection

The `searchedAt` field in the GET /search response is an ISO-8601 datetime string reflecting the time of the request (not a hardcoded value); successive requests separated by at least 1 ms return distinct values

The FlightResult type used in src/server.ts is imported from the SKY-002 type export (e.g. src/skyscanner/client.ts) and not redeclared inline — type definitions must not diverge between the client and server layers

stories.title: Implement SkyscannerClient class and interfaces
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts with the SkyscannerClient class, SearchParams and FlightResult interfaces, global-fetch-based searchFlights method, constructor key validation (including empty-string and precedence rules), HTTP error handling, parse-error handling, and strict opt-in mock mode via MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API='true'.

searchFlights rejects with an Error including the HTTP status code on 4xx/5xx responses; the Error message does not include the apiKey value anywhere

stories.title: Implement flight search CLI entry point (src/cli.ts)
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that parses --from, --to, --date, --adults from process.argv (no external deps), validates inputs, checks RAPIDAPI_KEY env, calls SkyscannerClient.searchFlights, and renders an aligned table with columns Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops.
